title: Word-edge association survives exact-length and coarse line-position controls but remains reproducible by a glyph chain
statement: A prospectively specified public sensitivity keeps both exact EVA-basic word lengths and each word's coarse line role fixed. Intact certain P words are shuffled only within (original line, exact glyph length, literal initial/medial/final/singleton role) cells. The original edge_length_cmi statistic and all pair boundaries stay unchanged. On the34 public practice evaluation pages, ZL has observed0.533009bits, position-preserving null mean0.441072, excess0.091937, p0.005; IT has0.512346, mean0.417240, excess0.095106, p0.005. Of4796/4740 adjacent pairs,3795/3806 (79.1%/80.3%) remain potentially movable. None of199 null draws reaches the observation. The fixed default line-chain control also passes both editions (p0.005 each), whereas independent unigram controls do not (p0.585 ZL,p0.47 IT). Thus coarse start/end roles and exact lengths do not explain the whole observed association, but a glyph chain explicitly modelling word-edge transitions reproduces it. This establishes neither semantics nor uniqueness to the manuscript. These are the same previously used public pages, not a fresh page sample. The unchanged PR673 fact draft remains unpublished and byte-identical; only local public diagnostics were run.
check: Keep the original PR673 metric and hidden fact specification frozen until human code review and merge. Treat this as a separate public sensitivity. If adding a trusted position-aware null, group words by literal original line, exact EVA-basic length and initial/medial/final/singleton role; keep uncertainties/empties as barriers, require >=30 potentially movable adjacent pairs and refuse an invariant null. Test line inventories, positional lengths, role inventories and fixed endpoints. Coarse medial role is not exact ordinal or physical spacing: further claims about those require separate plans. A line-chain control explicitly models edge transitions, so it shows mechanistic reproducibility, not spontaneous emergence or language. Register no hidden claim before trusted metric review.

plan.question: Does adjacent edge association survive a null preserving exact word lengths AND coarse line positions?
plan.metric: Unchanged edge_length_cmi: I(last glyph; next first glyph | exact left/right EVA-basic lengths), weighted by adjacent-pair count.
plan.primary_null: Permute certain nonempty P words only within (original line, exact EVA-basic length, original role) cells.
plan.roles: singleton if n=1; initial if k=0; final if k=n-1; medial otherwise. k and n from the literal original line, before filtering.
plan.baseline_null: Same permutation without role conditioning, reproducing PR673.
plan.sample: 34 public practice evaluation pages, separately ZL and IT; already used in prior analyses, not new independent pages.
plan.decision: Residual association supported only if primary one-sided plus-one p<=.01 in both editions, >=30 pairs are potentially movable and permuted statistic is not constant. Report all baseline and position-aware outcomes; no seed or threshold tuning.
plan.limits: Coarse word role, not exact ordinal, x coordinate, glyph position within word, or physical word spacing. One fixed seed per generator. Public sensitivity only; original fact bytes remain unchanged.

evidence.selfcheck: Analytical role fixture: literal endpoints, singleton/two-word lines, empty/uncertain barriers, EVA ch unit, and actual interior shuffle pass.
